description: Tests that the stack depth skill correctly runs asm-analyze stack-depth, interprets the JSON output, and reports worst-case depth, call paths, per-function frames, warnings, and optional budget verdicts. All functions are compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/CC2340R5/basic_ble.out.
note: Set $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT to your local BLE project root before running. Evals sd-5 and sd-6 instead use $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT, a fixture run_evals.sh stages from evals/fixtures/stale-artifact/. It needs arm-none-eabi-gcc and a loci CLI with `build fresh`; without either, run_evals.sh skips them by detecting the unexpanded placeholder (there is no `requires` key to set — the placeholder itself is the gate, so a typo cannot bypass it).

evals.prompt: Analyze the stack depth for GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble/freertos/ticlang/basic_ble.out. No stack budget — just show me the worst-case depth and the call path.
evals.expected_output: Runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --elf-path and --entry-functions GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent. Reports worst-case depth in bytes, the worst-case call path as a chain of function names, average depth, and per-function frame sizes along the worst path, then a conclusion table. Because no --stack-budget was provided, it does NOT report a usage percentage or a budget/threshold pass-fail check; the no-budget conclusion footer (Verdict: **PASS** — worst-case <N> bytes) may still appear per SKILL.md.

assertions.text: Response runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --elf-path pointing to basic_ble.out and --entry-functions GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent
assertions.description: Must use the stack-depth subcommand with the correct entry function

assertions.text: Response reports a worst-case depth in bytes (a specific number, not fabricated)
assertions.description: The core output: total accumulated stack bytes along the deepest path

assertions.text: Response shows a worst-case call path as a chain of function names (more than one function)
assertions.description: The path must show the actual chain from entry to deepest leaf

assertions.text: Response reports per-function frame sizes for functions along the worst path
assertions.description: Each function in the path should show its individual frame contribution

assertions.text: Response does NOT report a usage percentage or a budget/threshold check
assertions.description: No --stack-budget was provided, so usage % and the threshold pass/fail comparison must be absent (a no-budget 'worst-case <N> bytes' verdict line may still appear)

evals.prompt: Run stack depth analysis on GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble/freertos/ticlang/basic_ble.out with a stack budget of 768 bytes and a 50% threshold.
evals.expected_output: Runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --elf-path, --entry-functions, --stack-budget 768, and --threshold 50. Reports worst-case depth, usage as a percentage of 768 bytes, and a PASS or FAIL verdict against the 50% threshold (384 bytes). Also reports the worst-case path and per-function frames.

assertions.text: Response runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --stack-budget 768 and --threshold 50
assertions.description: Budget and threshold flags must be passed to enable the verdict

assertions.text: Response reports usage as a percentage of the 768-byte budget
assertions.description: Usage percentage is required when a budget is provided

assertions.text: Response includes a PASS or FAIL verdict
assertions.description: The verdict compares worst-case depth against 50% of 768 bytes (384 bytes)

assertions.text: Response shows the worst-case call path and per-function frame sizes
assertions.description: Full reporting is still required alongside the verdict

evals.prompt: Analyze stack depth for all root functions in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble/freertos/ticlang/basic_ble.out. Don't specify entry functions — let the tool auto-detect them.
evals.expected_output: Runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --elf-path but without --entry-functions, letting the tool auto-detect root functions. Reports per-function results for multiple entry points, each with worst-case depth, path, and frame sizes.

assertions.text: Response runs asm-analyze stack-depth without --entry-functions to auto-detect roots
assertions.description: Auto-detection mode should be used when no entry functions are specified

assertions.text: Response reports results for more than one function
assertions.description: A real ELF has multiple root functions; the tool should find and report them

assertions.text: Each reported function has a worst-case depth and path
assertions.description: Per-function reporting is required even in multi-function mode

evals.prompt: Analyze stack depth for osal_msg_send in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble/freertos/ticlang/basic_ble.out. I suspect there may be recursive calls in the chain. Use --max-recursion-depth 3.
evals.expected_output: Runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --entry-functions osal_msg_send and --max-recursion-depth 3. If recursion is detected, reports a warning about the recursive call and notes the depth is bounded to 3 iterations. If no recursion is found, reports the depth normally. Either way, the tool should handle the flag and report clearly.

assertions.text: Response runs asm-analyze stack-depth with --max-recursion-depth 3
assertions.description: The recursion depth flag must be passed through

assertions.text: Response reports the worst-case depth and path for osal_msg_send
assertions.description: Core analysis must complete regardless of recursion

assertions.text: If recursion is detected, response mentions it explicitly as a warning
assertions.description: Recursion warnings are critical for stack safety — they must be surfaced

evals.prompt: I just changed kernel_main in $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT/blink.c to call a new build_pattern() helper. Give me the worst-case stack depth for kernel_main against a 2048-byte budget. The project builds with `arm-none-eabi-gcc -g -nostartfiles -O0 -mcpu=cortex-m0plus -mthumb -Wl,-T,fixture.ld blink.c startup.c -o kernel.elf` from $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT.
evals.expected_output: This is the regression test for the reported bug: the tree contains kernel.elf linked BEFORE the edit (225 s older than blink.c, and it does not contain build_pattern or render_frame at all) plus a post-edit object at .loci-build/armv6-m/blink.o. Per Step 0 Pattern B the skill must gate on freshness (loci build fresh --elf, or data.source_provenance on a loci elf call), find kernel.elf stale, and NOT report numbers from it. It must then rebuild: relinking with the given command line is the correct move, because measuring the fresh .o instead would lose the call edge (an unapplied R_ARM_THM_CALL relocation) and report kernel_main as 8 B / PASS while hiding a 3072-byte buffer. After the relink, kernel_main's worst case is 3120 bytes along kernel_main -> build_pattern -> render_frame, i.e. 152.3% of the 2048-byte budget, verdict FAIL. The report must carry the mandatory Artifact: provenance line naming the binary actually measured. A run that reports 0.4% PASS (the stale ELF) or 8 B PASS (the bare .o) is a FAIL of this eval.

assertions.text: Response checks artifact freshness before reporting numbers — runs `loci build fresh --elf` or reads `source_provenance` / `stale` from a loci elf envelope
assertions.description: The gate must run at all; this is the defect the tester reported

assertions.text: Response identifies kernel.elf as stale / older than blink.c, and does NOT present its numbers as the answer
assertions.description: Detecting staleness but reporting the stale numbers anyway is still the bug

assertions.text: Response rebuilds — relinks the project (or compiles and links) rather than measuring the bare .loci-build object as the answer
assertions.description: A relocatable .o loses cross-call edges, so switching to it reports 8 B / PASS: fresh artifact, confidently wrong answer

assertions.text: Response reports a worst-case depth of 3120 bytes for kernel_main
assertions.description: 3120 = 8 + 3088 + 24, confirmed independently by gcc -fstack-usage; it is only obtainable from a relinked ELF, so it proves both that staleness was caught and that the relink happened

assertions.text: Response reports the worst-case path as kernel_main -> build_pattern -> render_frame
assertions.description: The call chain only resolves in a linked binary

assertions.text: Response reports a FAIL verdict at roughly 152% of the 2048-byte budget
assertions.description: The budget verdict must invert relative to the stale artifact's PASS

assertions.text: Response includes an `Artifact:` provenance line naming which binary was measured and when it was built
assertions.description: The durable safety net: even if selection regresses, the reader can see what was measured

evals.prompt: Run a stack depth analysis on kernel_main in $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT/.loci-build/armv6-m/relinked.elf with a stack budget of 2048 bytes. If that file does not exist, first link it with `arm-none-eabi-gcc -g -nostartfiles -O0 -mcpu=cortex-m0plus -mthumb -Wl,-T,fixture.ld blink.c startup.c -o .loci-build/armv6-m/relinked.elf` from $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT.
evals.expected_output: A current, correctly linked ELF whose kernel_main reaches a 3072-byte stack buffer through build_pattern. Frame sizes are kernel_main 8, build_pattern 3088, render_frame 24 (gcc -fstack-usage agrees), so the worst case is 3120 bytes: 152.3% of the 2048-byte budget, verdict FAIL, path kernel_main -> build_pattern -> render_frame, largest frame build_pattern at ~99% of the total. This is the frame-sizing half of the regression: before asmslicer 1.1.1, compute_frame_size matched decimal-only immediates while capstone renders >= 10 in hex, so every frame collapsed to ~8 bytes and this exact case reported 16 B / 0.8% / PASS. Any PASS verdict, or a worst case anywhere near 8-24 bytes, is a FAIL of this eval.

assertions.text: Response reports a worst-case depth of 3120 bytes for kernel_main (not ~8, ~16 or ~24)
assertions.description: A near-zero figure means frame sizing regressed to the decimal-immediate bug

assertions.text: Response reports a FAIL verdict against the 2048-byte budget at roughly 152% usage
assertions.description: The budget verdict must be FAIL — the code overflows the budget by 2x

assertions.text: Response identifies build_pattern as the dominant frame at about 3088 bytes
assertions.description: The 3072-byte buffer plus 16 bytes of prologue; it is 99% of the worst path

assertions.text: Response reports the worst-case path as kernel_main -> build_pattern -> render_frame
assertions.description: All three frames must be summed along the path, not just the entry frame

assertions.text: Response includes an `Artifact:` provenance line naming which binary was measured and when it was built
assertions.description: Mandatory for every Pattern B report, fresh artifact or not
